preview: The write-off follows ownership.

• Term loans secured by equipment
• Conditional sales contracts
• $1 buyout leases

A one-line answer for each helps us match files correctly.

body:

We're a Canadian commercial finance brokerage, and we expect a wave of equipment requests from Canadian businesses ahead of their year-ends.

Do you fund Canadian borrowers today? If so, I'd like to send you deals. If not yet, I'd like to understand what it would take.

name: YE26 Write-Off · US Lenders · 02 · Thu Nov 12 · The Canadian write-off in plain terms
subject: The Canadian write-off in plain terms
preview: What qualifies, what doesn't, and why it matters to lenders.
body:
Hi {{first_name}},

A short summary of the proposed Productivity Mega Deduction:

• 100% write-off in the year the asset is put into use
• Most equipment, machinery, computers and software acquired on or after September 15, 2026
• Used equipment qualifies if bought from an unrelated seller
• Excludes buildings, goodwill and certain vehicles

The government says it cuts the tax rate on new business investment from 13% to 6.4%. For lenders, it means more Canadian owners wanting to buy equipment, with financing structures where they keep ownership.

Todd Werboweski
Director, Boreal Financial

subject: What the write-off could look like in real numbers
preview: A $250,000 example.
body:
Hi {{first_name}},

An illustration: a business buys a $250,000 machine and finances it over five years at about 9%. Payments come to roughly $62,000 a year.

If the full $250,000 is written off this year, the tax saving is about $27,500 for an Alberta company paying the small-business rate, or about $57,500 at the general rate.

In that example, the saving covers a large share of the first year's payments. Your numbers will differ; your accountant can run them.

The Boreal Financial team
